name: SentinelBench reference agent (Magentic-UI browser agent with wait_for)

system_prompt_style.note: Agent code not in pinned repo; paper does not show the system prompt construction.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: the model receives a screenshot of the current browser state along with a brief description, then selects from a set of browser tools such as click, type, scroll, andvisit URL

observation_format.evidence_quote: the model receives a screenshot of the current browser state along with a brief description

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: the agent follows a simple tool-calling loop

tool_count.note: Paper lists 'browser tools such as click, type, scroll, and visit URL' plus sleep/wait_for and terminate, but not an exhaustive count.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: selects from a set of browser tools such as click, type, scroll, andvisit URL
edit_primitive.note: Browser-only agent; no file editing tool described.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: we do not require a particular agent or browser framework, such as Playwright, nor do we assume any particular observation format or modality
protocol_standardization.note: No protocol mentioned anywhere in repo or paper; harness invokes agent as a shell subprocess.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: At each iteration, the model receives a screenshot of the current browser state along with a brief description, then selects from a set of browser tools

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the agent follows a simple tool-calling loop

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: we pair three multimodal models: GPT-5.4 with ‘low’ reasoning, Qwen 3.5:9B, and GPT-4o, with a web browsing agent adapted from our work on Magentic-UI

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: the agent follows a simple tool-calling loop

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: the user provides a shell command template with placeholders for the task prompt and starting webpage URL
human_in_loop.note: Fully automated subprocess evaluation; no approval step.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The loop continues until the model stops making tool calls or invokes aterminatetool.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: For each task, the evaluation harness fills in these values, invokes the command, runs the simulation, and computes metrics.
long_term_memory.note: Each task is an independent subprocess; no cross-run memory described.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Execute scenarios (resumable: tasks with an existing result are skipped)
state_persistence.note: Harness-level skip of completed tasks, not agent state resume.

self_verification.evidence_quote: This endpoint executes the previously saved SQL query against the database to determine whether the task was successful.
self_verification.note: Benchmark-side grading only; no self-verification inside the agent is described. wait_for uses an LLM check of page diffs against the condition.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: The loop continues until the model stops making tool calls or invokes aterminatetool.

rollback.note: Environment reset between tasks is harness-side, not an agent rollback mechanism.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: The loop continues until the model stops making tool calls or invokes aterminatetool.
termination_condition.note: model_declared is the agent-side condition; the harness also kills the subprocess on a wall-clock timeout (see F3). max_steps not explicitly evidenced — treat as uncertain.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Agents may therefore produce anoptionalcosts.jsonsidecarfiledeclaringthenumberofinputtokens,outputtokens,andtoolcallsused during the task.

timeouts.evidence_quote: The harness sizes each task's subprocess timeout as `kill_at_wall = MAX_CONDITION_AT / speed_factor + REACTION_WINDOW`.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The harness discovers every scenario JSON, runs each one against your agent as a subprocess, and collects results.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Command to launch your agent. Placeholders are substituted per task
filesystem_access.note: Agent runs as an unrestricted host subprocess.

network_policy.note: No network restriction mechanism appears in the repo or paper.

permission_model.evidence_quote: any web-capable agent that can be invoked from the terminal can be evaluated

tracing.note: results.json plus output.txt agent stdout per task.

replayability.note: Logs only; no replay path. run_simulation.py replays scenario events, not agent trajectories.

guardrails.evidence_quote: we do not require a particular agent or browser framework, such as Playwright, nor do we assume any particular observation format or modality
guardrails.note: No filters or action policies described in harness or agent.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a benchmark of 10 high-fidelity web-app replicas that tests whether an agent can *wait*, *monitor*, and *act* only when a condition is met

open_source.evidence_quote: This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
open_source.note: Benchmark repo is MIT; the reference agent itself is not in this repo.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we pair three multimodal models: GPT-5.4 with ‘low’ reasoning, Qwen 3.5:9B, and GPT-4o

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: a web browsing agent adapted from our work on Magentic-UI Mozannar et al. (2025a)
primary_artifact.note: The reference agent's code is not in the pinned sentinel_environments repo; coded from the paper.

first_release_date.note: Basis: first (and pinned) tag of the benchmark repo.

pinned_version.note: Only the short hash is given in the evidence.
